subject: Geo-failover insurance & uptime crediting — pricing proposal
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@brightgrid.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: regional outage insurance + uptime crediting

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: we’re putting together an operational risk budget for the next contract year and procurement asked us to price in a ‘geo-failover insurance’ add-on — essentially a paid SLA enhancement that provides deeper credits if a regional blackout impacts our primary region and we need to fail over across regions.

Key asks: can you outline how Redwood would structure credits for a regional outage (single-region blackout) vs a zonal/local outage? We care about the math (how credits are calculated against monthly spend), whether credits are capped, and whether there’s an insurance-like surcharge (flat fee add-on) to reduce credit percentages. Also, what does 24/7 escalation coverage cost vs business-hours-only?

We have an internal target availability: baseline 99.9% for primary region; we’re exploring committing to 99.95 if the economics look reasonable.

Timeline: procurement needs a formal quote and the crediting mechanics by end of week (Aug 28). Can you include an example calculation for a $75k monthly committed spend? Also loop in finance/legal as needed.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Ops, BrightGrid

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: regional outage insurance + uptime crediting

Tom — thanks for the clear brief. Attaching a compact pricing grid (SLA_PRICING_GRID_v3.xlsx) that shows two recommended options and the sample math for $75k/mo. High level here so procurement has something to share with finance quickly: 

Option A — Failover Insurance (recommended for pilot)
- Add-on: flat monthly surcharge = 8% of committed spend
- Uptime target uplift: base 99.9% -> optional 99.95% (+ managed rollout)
- Credit on breach: regional blackout = 30% of monthly committed spend, zonal/local outage = standard 10%
- Cap: credit capped to 100% of monthly committed spend (no multi-month backfills)
- Escalation: 24/7 rapid-response add-on = +3% surcharge, else business-hours only included

Option B — Conservative Crediting (lower surcharge)
- Add-on: flat monthly surcharge = 4% of committed spend
- Uptime target uplift optional
- Credit on breach: regional blackout = 20%, zonal/local outage = 8%
- Cap: same 100% per month cap
- Escalation: 24/7 = +2% surcharge

Sample math (Option A, $75k/mo committed):
- Base subscription: $75,000
- Failover insurance (8%): $6,000
- 24/7 escalation (+3%): $2,250
- Total monthly invoice: $83,250
- If a regional blackout occurs and we fail over -> credit = 30% * $75,000 = $22,500 applied to the invoice for the affected month

Notes and caveats:
- Credits apply to committed spend, not overages or transient burst usage.
- We propose a 3-month pilot discount of 20% on the add-on surcharge to validate behavior (we can show impact in the attached sheet).
- DocuSign SOW draft included when you’re ready.

Next steps: Jonas and Karthik — can you confirm margin floor and legal redline on cap/retroactive credit? Tom — if this looks directionally correct I’ll prepare a formal quote and a short memo explaining credit calculus for procurement.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Inquiry: regional outage insurance + uptime crediting — quick internal ask

Forwarding Tom’s ask and my draft options. Quick internal checklist:
- Margin: we need to keep gross margin >= 55% at quoted surcharges after pilot discount.
- Cap language: legal is pushing to keep cap at 100%/month; procurement may ask for 2x monthly in aggregate — can we tolerate that?
- Escalation staffing: overnight 24/7 escalation increases staffing costs; Karthik, can you confirm the incremental monthly ops cost per $75k seat?

Proposed negotiation posture: offer Option A (8% + 3% for 24/7) with a 3-month pilot 20% discount on the add-on. For procurement pressure, offer Option B as fallback with slightly worse credits but lower surcharge.

Redlined points to anticipate from legal/procurement:
- Retroactive credit windows (we propose 30 days)
- Whether credits are refundable cash vs invoice credit (we prefer invoice credit to avoid cash outflow)
- Definition of regional blackout (we define as complete regional management plane & N+1 infra unavail for >1 hour)

If you both sign off, I’ll put final numbers in HubSpot and prep the DocuSign SOW. Deal id: BG-2026-0521.

—Rachel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@brightgrid.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, BrightGrid Finance <finance@brightgrid.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final proposal: Geo-failover insurance & credits (BG-2026-0521)

Tom / BrightGrid team — thanks for your patience while we worked the internals. Finalizing numbers per Rachel’s note and internal sign-off: 

Final Offer (pilot terms — 3 months):
- Option A (Recommended):
  - Add-on surcharge: 8% of committed monthly spend (pilot discount 20% for first 3 months -> effective 6.4%)
  - 24/7 escalation: +3% (pilot discount applies to add-on portion only; escalation billed at full rate)
  - Credits: regional blackout = 30% of committed monthly spend; zonal/local outage = 10%
  - Cap: credits capped at 100% of monthly committed spend per month; credit issued as invoice credit (not cash refund)
  - Retroactive window: 30 days from event occurrence for credit requests

- Option B (Alternate):
  - Add-on surcharge: 4% (no pilot discount)
  - 24/7 escalation: +2%
  - Credits: regional blackout = 20%; zonal/local outage = 8%

Example (Option A, $75k/mo committed, pilot month):
- Subscription: $75,000
- Add-on (6.4% pilot-effective): $4,800
- 24/7 escalation (3%): $2,250
- Invoice total: $82,050
- If regional blackout occurs -> credit = 30% * $75,000 = $22,500 applied as invoice credit for that month

Operational points:
- Definition of regional blackout will be codified in SOW (we’ll include monitoring logs & incident review as evidence).
- Credits apply to committed spend only. Overage token usage excluded.

Next steps:
1) Rachel: I’ve created the HubSpot record and attached the finalized pricing grid (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890).
2) Tom / Finance: if approved, we’ll send the DocuSign SOW (attached) for signature and onboard the pilot.
3) If procurement needs a different cap, escalate to me and Jonas and we’ll review trade-offs (we can consider a blended cap for annualized contracts).

Thanks — looking forward.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments referenced: SLA_PRICING_GRID_v3.xlsx (pricing table and sample calculations), DocuSign_SOW_BrightGrid.pdf
